name: lexponent
description: Lexponent connects your AI assistant to federal and state court rules, statutes, and more. Build filing checklists, review a draft filing against the rules, map the procedural timeline that follows a trigger event, generate court-specific practice guides, and get cited answers to procedural questions. Every statement links to the rule it rests on, so you can verify in one click. Requires a Lexponent account.

interface.longDescription:
Lexponent connects ChatGPT to federal and state court rules, statutes, and more. Build filing checklists, review a draft filing against the rules, map the procedural timeline that follows a trigger event, generate court-specific practice guides, and get cited answers to procedural questions. Every statement links to the rule it rests on, so you can verify in one click. Requires a Lexponent account.

Lexponent is built for attorneys, paralegals, legal secretaries, and the filing and docketing staff who need to know exactly what specific courts require. It covers all federal courts and a growing list of states' court rules and statutes.
defaultPrompt: How do I demand a jury trial in the Northern District of California?
Give me a filing checklist for a motion to compel further responses in LA Superior Court.
What is the deadline to file a notice of appeal from a civil judgment in federal court?

positive.description: Answer a federal procedural question from rule text.
positive.prompt: How do I demand a jury trial in the Northern District of California?
positive.expected_behavior: States the written-demand requirement and 14-day deadline from Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 38(b) and the Northern District's Civil Local Rule 3-6. Each rule carries a link produced by cite. No rule is stated without a citation.

positive.description: Retrieve a specific California statute by its identifier.
positive.prompt: Show me the text of California Code of Civil Procedure section 1008.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Code of Civil Procedure section 1008 (applications to reconsider) by title, returns its text or an accurate summary of each subdivision, and links the section with cite.

positive.description: Build a filing checklist for a California superior court motion.
positive.prompt: Give me a filing checklist for a motion to compel further responses in LA Superior Court.
positive.tools_triggered: list_rulesets, list_documents, search_rules, grep_rules, find_rule_by_title, cite
positive.expected_behavior: Builds the checklist from the Code of Civil Procedure section for the discovery device at issue (sections 2030.300, 2031.310 or 2033.290, including the 45-day notice deadline and the section 2016.040 meet-and-confer declaration), California Rules of Court rule 3.1345 (separate statement), and the general motion rules. Applies only Los Angeles local rules that govern motions and does not invent a local motion-to-compel rule. Every item is cited.

positive.description: Search local rules for a phrase and handle a phrase that appears only in variant wording.
positive.prompt: Which Central District of California local rules mention meet and confer?
positive.expected_behavior: Reports that the literal phrase appears only as 'met and conferred' in L.R. 54-2, broadens the search to confer and conference-of-counsel language, and lists L.R. 7-3, 16-2, 26-1, 37-1, 37-2, 54-2 and 79-5, each with a cite link. Does not list rules from other courts.

positive.description: Handle a jurisdiction Lexponent does not cover.
positive.prompt: What is the page limit for a motion in Wyoming state district court?
positive.expected_behavior: list_rulesets returns an error naming the covered jurisdictions. The answer says Wyoming is not covered and gives no uncited rule or page limit.

negative.description: Case-law research is outside Lexponent's corpus of rules and statutes.
negative.prompt: Find California cases holding that a non-compete clause is unenforceable.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not present Lexponent results as case law and does not invent case citations. Explains that Lexponent covers court rules and statutes, not judicial opinions.

negative.description: Filing and service are actions Lexponent cannot take; all tools are read-only.
negative.prompt: File my opposition brief with the court and serve opposing counsel.
negative.expected_behavior: Does not claim to file or serve anything. Explains that Lexponent can only look up and cite rules, and may offer a filing checklist instead.

negative.description: Predicting a ruling is outside the rules corpus.
negative.prompt: Will Judge Smith grant my motion for summary judgment?
negative.expected_behavior: Does not call Lexponent tools to predict an outcome or profile a judge. Explains that Lexponent answers what the rules require, not how a court will rule.

review.commerce_description: Lexponent does not sell products or process payments in ChatGPT.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: rule questions and filing checklists, with every rule cited to its source document.

description.short: Cited answers and filing checklists from court rules and statutes
description.full:
Lexponent gives your assistant the text of the procedural rules that govern litigation: rules of court, local rules, and the statutes they rely on. Ask a procedural question and get an answer grounded in the rule text, with each point linked to the page of the source rule document it came from. Ask for a filing checklist and get the formatting and content requirements for that filing in that court, each one cited, then have the assistant check your draft against it.

Who it's for: attorneys, paralegals, legal secretaries, and filing and docketing staff who need to know what a court's rules require.

Coverage: federal courts and courts in a set of states, including local rules where Lexponent has them. A question about a jurisdiction Lexponent does not cover gets an answer that says so instead of an uncited one.

Limitations: Lexponent retrieves and cites rules and statutes. It does not search case law, file or serve documents, add dates to a calendar, or predict how a court will rule. Rules change, so open the linked source before you file. Lexponent is a research tool, not legal advice. All tools are read-only. A Lexponent account is required.
